title: What If You Watched Dinosaurs Through a Telescope?

scenes.text: What if you could watch the dinosaurs live? The light from them is still out there.
Light from Earth 65 million years ago is now about 65 million light years away.
An observer there would see Earth as it was, around the time the last dinosaurs died.
But to make out a single dinosaur, the lens would need to be about four light years across.
That is wider than the distance from our Sun to the nearest star.
Such a lens would collapse into a black hole, so the dinosaurs' light exists, but we can never watch it.

description:
What if you could watch dinosaurs through a telescope?
Their light is still traveling through space, but seeing a single animal would need a lens about four light years wide.
